title: Clearer Through the Pinhole

patient.name: Ms Wong Hui Shan
patient.presenting_complaint: Blurred distance vision; here for a visual acuity check

history.hpc: Ms Wong reports her distance vision has become blurry over the past year, especially for signboards. She says: 'Far things blur, but when I squeeze my eyes a bit, can see clearer.' Squinting that improves vision hints at a refractive cause. She wears no correction. The PSA must measure distance VA on the Modified LogMAR chart and apply the pinhole.
history.social_hx: Retail assistant. Long screen time. Non-smoker.

investigations.va_distance: Modified LogMAR distance VA: RE 6/18, LE 6/24 unaided, right eye tested first. As VA was reduced, the pinhole was applied and improved vision in both eyes towards 6/6, suggesting a refractive cause.
investigations.pinhole: Both eyes improve with pinhole — points to a refractive (correctable with glasses) cause rather than a media or retinal cause.

diagnosis: Reduced distance VA that improves with the pinhole, suggesting uncorrected refractive error (likely myopia) in a young patient — for refraction and spectacles. The PSA competency is correct LogMAR VA measurement, appropriate pinhole use, and interpreting the improvement as a refractive clue; the prescription is set by the doctor/optometrist.

immediate: Perform distance VA on the Modified LogMAR chart, right eye first, with hand hygiene and an alcohol-wiped occluder
Ask the patient to read all 5 letters per line, stopping when she cannot read all 5
Apply the pinhole because VA is reduced, and record the improvement
Perform NCT for IOP as part of the workup
Document unaided VA, pinhole VA, and IOP for both eyes
Explain that pinhole improvement suggests glasses are likely to help
follow_up: Doctor/optometrist to perform subjective refraction and prescribe spectacles
Discuss spectacles vs contact lenses with the optometrist
Advise return if vision changes further
patient_education: Explain that her vision improving with the pinhole suggests she needs glasses (short-sightedness)
Reassure her this is common and easily corrected
Explain the doctor/optometrist will fine-tune the exact prescription

key_points: Establishes gradual blurred distance vision and that squinting helps
Notes the family history of myopia
Confirms she wears no correction currently
Rules out red-flag symptoms (pain, sudden loss, flashes/floaters)
Performs LogMAR distance VA correctly, right eye first, reading all 5 letters per line
Applies the pinhole because VA is reduced and records the improvement
Performs and documents NCT for IOP
Documents unaided and pinhole VA for both eyes
Recognises pinhole improvement as suggesting a refractive cause
Links the symptoms (squinting helps, family myopia) to likely myopia
Distinguishes a refractive cause from a media/retinal cause
Defers the final prescription to the doctor/optometrist
Documents unaided VA, pinhole VA, and IOP accurately
Explains the pinhole result to the patient in simple terms
Refers to the doctor/optometrist for refraction
Reassures the patient that glasses are likely to help
